subject: Learning Methods
title: Elaborative Encoding
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Elaborative Encoding.

hook.text: Two students study the same fact. One reads it. The other connects it to something she already knows.

buildup.text: Elaborative encoding means linking new information to existing knowledge. It weaves a richer web.

discovery.text: The more connections you create, the more retrieval paths exist. Multiple paths mean easier recall.

twist.text: This is why analogies are so powerful. Comparing mitochondria to a power plant builds instant hooks.

climax.text: Ask yourself: What does this remind me of? How does it relate to what I already know?

punchline.text: Connect the new to the known. Memory webs hold tight.

quiz.question: Why does elaborative encoding improve memory?
options: It creates multiple retrieval paths through connections
